“The Music Man,” I’m sorry to say, does not live up to our oversize expectations.

More’s the pity, then, that this undeniably polished production, with its ticket-sales-galvanizing star, Hugh Jackman, proves to be a sadly mechanical, overproduced and overdesigned revival of a musical that needs tender care to allow its undeniable charms to bloom.
This revival has been in the works seemingly forever.

But there’s nothing simplistic about The Music Man, and this slightly zany production, deeply felt and deeply funny, sells the show’s intelligent warmth with a persuasiveness to rival Harold Hill himself.
On the other hand, it doesn’t quite rise to blue-ribbon garden-show winner.

Everything onstage is pure Broadway gold, fine-tuned to the gods and played to the back of the house.

So, scrubbed clean of anything that might offend the supersensitive, costing as much as a cross-country flight, and, in some views, lacking the chiaroscuro of darkness mingled with light, The Music Man still comes out a winner.
While this may not be the perfect Music Man, it’s joyful enough to bring a much-needed lift to a beleaguered and battered Broadway and should bring in audiences for years to come.
